sections.description: This section details the patient's clinical history, surgical context, and the timeline of adverse events, establishing the initial clinical problem and identifying key risk factors such as preoperative heparin exposure.
subtopics: Patient demographics, cardiac history, and surgical procedure details
Timeline of platelet count decline relative to intraoperative and preoperative heparin exposure
Recognition of neurological symptoms and cerebral infarct imaging findings
Initial laboratory evaluation including CBC, coagulation profile, and exclusion of hemorrhage

sections.section_title: Pathophysiology of Classic and Autoimmune HIT
sections.description: This section provides the necessary background on the immunological mechanisms of Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia, distinguishing between classic heparin-dependent HIT and the rarer autoimmune HIT (aHIT) phenotype.
subtopics: Mechanism of PF4-heparin complex formation and IgG antibody generation
Platelet activation via Fc receptor clustering in classic HIT
Distinctive features of autoimmune HIT including heparin-independent platelet activation
Impact of prior heparin sensitization on the timing of thrombocytopenia onset

sections.description: This section explains the diagnostic reasoning process, focusing on the differential diagnosis of postoperative thrombocytopenia and the nuanced interpretation of immunological assays used to confirm aHIT.
subtopics: Differential diagnosis for severe post-cardiac surgery thrombocytopenia (e.g., TTP, drug-induced)
Interpretation of PF4/polyanion ELISA screening results and sensitivity
Analysis of Serotonin Release Assay (SRA) profiles including heparin-independent release
Understanding atypical SRA results and partial resistance to Fc receptor blockade

sections.description: This section outlines the treatment strategies employed, discussing the rationale for selecting specific anticoagulants and adjunctive therapies in the context of severe thrombocytopenia and thrombosis.
subtopics: Selection criteria for non-heparin anticoagulants (Argatroban vs. Fondaparinux)
Role and dosing of high-dose intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) in aHIT
Monitoring therapeutic efficacy using fibrinogen and d-dimer trends
Rationale for switching anticoagulants based on clinical and laboratory response

sections.description: This section reviews the patient's recovery trajectory, the evolution of serological markers over time, and summarizes key clinical lessons for managing atypical HIT presentations.
subtopics: Timeline of platelet count recovery and neurological resolution
Evolution of SRA reactivity profiles from heparin-independent to heparin-dependent
Clinical pearls regarding early-onset HIT following preoperative catheterization
Long-term anticoagulation management and follow-up after HIT resolution
